note: Controlled benchmark of the engine at commit 98cff9d (v0.7.0 plus the defect fixes, a curated two-tone colour layer, and five new art directions shadcn-mono, material-tonal, swiss-grid, noir-luxe, pastel-play with style routing). Haiku 5.5 without vs with the MCP, identical SPEC.md, same 60-call budget, four never-seen domains (tideline surf school, hollis architects, brightwater vet clinic, stockroom inventory app), engine frozen for the run. RESULT: engine 2/8, judged more template-like in 6/8: the best generator result so far but still a clear loss. Both engine wins were pages whose hero is a specific product UI mockup (brightwater clinic day sheet, stockroom stock screen). The new swiss-grid style was chosen by the matcher for the architects brief and LOST both pairs: judges called it a loud red-and-black startup look with a generic flat house drawing, a broken final CTA headline, a lopsided testimonials grid and an uneven hero. The spec forbids external images for both arms, so the photo, logo-prompt and placeholder tools were not exercised. COST: the MCP arm used about 17% more tokens, about 45% more tool calls and about 70% more wall-clock time than the baseline arm this run. DEFECTS named by agents and judges (to fix): swiss-grid CTA and testimonials layout; the schedule hero kind rendered empty; a duplicate id=features in the generated markup that the gate did not flag; last-section padding 31px against 104px elsewhere; brief_template has no good category for service businesses (surf school and services both returned the SaaS template, and search_design_references rejected the category); an agent could not find a logos caption field. CONFOUNDS: the Stockroom MCP agent made one failed send_message call to another session (nothing was sent); several agents deleted their own scratch files; the Stockroom MCP agent used the older field-notes style by its own patch, so the new styles were exercised only on Hollis. NOT deployed to Vercel (no VERCEL_TOKEN in this environment).
